findings.module: 7. User-Installed Root CA Certificates (TLS Interception Check)
findings.message: CRITICAL: User-installed Root CA certificate found in /data/misc/user/0/cacerts-added/!
findings.remediation_title: User-Installed Root CA Certificate (TLS Interception / MITM Proxy)
findings.threat_analysis: A rogue certificate installed in user credentials allows attackers or spyware to decrypt and intercept all HTTPS traffic, credentials, and encrypted communications in real-time.

remediation_steps.phase: 1. Delete User Certificate in Android Settings
remediation_steps.action: Navigate to Settings -> Security -> Encryption & Credentials -> User Credentials, select the certificate, and tap 'Remove'.
Check that the user cert directory is empty.

findings.threat_analysis: Applications installed outside official app stores bypass automated security vetting and frequently contain repackaged spyware or banking trojans.

remediation_steps.action: Remove the unverified package via ADB.
Ensure 'Install Unknown Apps' is globally revoked in Android Settings -> Apps -> Special App Access.
